title: Telemetry-driven region routing with network health scoring
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a region-selection policy that uses live latency telemetry (p50 and p95) plus a composite network health score to pick the best region for a request. This ticket covers metric selection, scoring algorithm, config knobs for routing policies (latency vs cost vs affinity), simulation harness, implementation in the router, and a safe rollout plan with observability and fallbacks. The policy must be pluggable so Console routing rules and Dedicated customer overrides can opt in/out. It should also be compatible with model-variant fallback (e.g., quantized model in same region or cross-region standard model fallback).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Router selects region according to documented scoring rules in production canary traffic; 2) p50/p95 aggregation pipeline emits region-level metrics used by score (Datadog/Prometheus); 3) Routing decision unit tests and simulators show >=90% alignment with offline golden policy under test traces; 4) Canary rollout shows no more than 2x increase in error budget consumption for affected customers; 5) Documentation and Console UI controls for policy are merged.
tasks: 1. Finalize metric set and normalization formula; 2. Implement scoring function in router service; 3. Add telemetry exporters for region p50/p95 and network loss indicators; 4. Create simulator to replay production traces and validate decisions; 5. Add config schema and Console toggle; 6. Integrate model-variant fallbacks and tie to scoring thresholds; 7. End-to-end test and canary; 8. Create dashboards and alerts; 9. Post-deploy review and rollback runbook.
design_notes: We prioritize tail-latency (p95) but keep p50 to avoid thrashing on transient hotspots. Scoring formula prototype: score(region) = 0.65 * normalize(p95_ms) + 0.25 * normalize(p50_ms) + 0.1 * network_penalty where network_penalty = clamp( (packet_loss_pct * 100) + (tcp_retransmits_per_min * 0.5), 0, 1) converted to same 0-1 scale. Normalization bounds use rolling 99th percentile per region over last 24h (min-max map). Lower score = better. Policy will pick lowest score if below absolute latency cap (default 600ms); otherwise fallback to next best region or model variant. Config knobs: p95_weight, p50_weight, packet_loss_threshold, absolute_latency_cap_ms, cross_region_cost_penalty. Metrics source: region aggregation in telemetry-service (pipeline ENG-6100).
implementation_plan: Phase A (local simulation): add scoring lib and run against 7 days of prod traces; Phase B (router integration): expose scoring via feature flag in router config, wire to realtime metric cache; Phase C (canary): route 1% traffic for 48h, monitor; Phase D (gradual ramp): 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with SLO gates. Implementation touches router-service, telemetry-service, and console-api. Key PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/247, github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/781, github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/412.
test_plan: Unit tests for normalization and score calculation. Integration test where synthetic region metrics drive deterministic decisions. Replay tests: run 72-hour production trace through simulator to compare decisions between baseline (latency-first simple p95 comparator) and new scoring; assert better tail latency or no regression in error rate. Canary monitoring: p50/p95 per-customer, request error rate, model fallback count, cost delta estimate. Automated rollback triggers: +20% sustained error rate or +15% latency p95 regression for >10m.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag off in prod; 2) Merge behind flag; 3) Enable for internal accounts only for one day; 4) Canary 1% traffic for 48h with SRE on call; 5) Evaluate metrics and expand to 5% then 25% if no gates violated; 6) 100% if stable. If cross-region traffic increases cost above threshold, reduce cross_region_cost_penalty or disable cross-region fallback per customer via Dedicated policy. Publish runbook in Confluence and link in comments.
risks: 1) Oscillation: frequent score changes could cause flapping—mitigation: add hysteresis and min-route-stay time (default 30s). 2) Metric pipeline lag causing stale decisions—mitigation: include 'metric_age' field and prefer regions with fresher data; if data older than threshold, fall back to affinity option. 3) Cost surge due to cross-region fallbacks—mitigation: per-customer cost caps. 4) Incompatible with Dedicated reserved routing—mitigation: Dedicated customers must explicitly allow cross-region fallback. 5) Security: ensure telemetry signals do not leak customer IDs—reviewed with security team if required.
